text:
One day she died again… I loved her,

but without remedy she died that day…

—Come back, Rabbi, come back!… I cried—

but the blond Rabbi did not return.


The girl passed twenty centuries dead,

Palestine's Capernaum died,

and my soul, useless and desolate,

wept immortally over the ruins.


And I loved her, loved her… Her whiteness

I sought in the white nebula,

her hair amid the dark night

and her rose color in the West…


And at last I found her… Hidden among the tulle

of a sunset, there she was;

her motionless flesh between two blues

inaugurated the first star…


And I found her whiter still,

floating in the blue, unclothed,

how white she was like that!… my girl

had twenty centuries of whiteness…


I cried to Love then… Good voices

said from far away: “He has heard you!”

I cried to eternal Love… and at my side

the white girl was scarcely a cloud…


Love came. The heavens fell silent,

his light step silenced the sphere,

eternal love came barefoot,

the hair of his head ripened wheat…


“She is not dead… She sleeps!” And he commanded her:

—Rise!

and she rose, slender with martyrdom,

and a voice climbed her throat

like a bee leaving a lily.


And she has returned to me… her dark hair,

her same voice… but in her cold hand,

with twenty centuries of kneading whiteness,

the fear of dying one day persists….

translation.title: She Died Again One Day...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the resurrection-like return, the repeated whiteness, and the source’s ellipses and abrupt commands.
